rep (4 levels, R1 to R4) is a design factor by the five-level rule: four reps of a single-drill trial, below five levels and fitted as fixed blocks in the help's lm(yield ~ 0 + gen + rep + cov).

rep (3 levels, R1 to R3) is a design factor by the five-level rule: three reps of an RCB trial, below five levels and fitted as fixed in the help's lm(twhite ~ rep + gen) (Gomez and Gomez 1984, table 7.21).
rep (3 levels, R1 to R3) is a design factor by the five-level rule: three reps, below five levels, and the help's glm(prop ~ rate, binomial) has no rep term.

Site (4 levels: AshleyRails, Caldicot, IsleThorns, Llanedyrn) is a design factor by the five-level rule: four find sites in Great Britain, below five levels and fitted as fixed in the SAS manual's MANOVA.
Block (4 levels, 1 to 4) is a design factor by the five-level rule: four blocks of a randomized block design, below five levels and fitted as fixed in the MANOVA of Friendly 2006.

operator (4 levels, op1 to op4) and day (4 levels, day1 to day4) are design factors by the five-level rule: the rows and columns of a four-by-four Latin square, below five levels, and the page states no model.
district (4 levels, 1 to 4) is a design factor by the five-level rule: four Exeter study districts, below five levels; no documented random district effect.
plate (4 levels, 1 to 4) is a design factor by the five-level rule: four ceramic plates of an incomplete block design, below five levels, and the page states no model.
site (4 levels: 1_UM, 2_IU, 3_UK, 4_Case) is a design factor by the five-level rule: the trial's four study centers, below five levels, and no documented model fits site as random.
Clinic (4 levels: KY, MN, MS, NY) is a design factor by the five-level rule: the trial's four enrollment centers, below five levels and used as strata of the log-rank test, not as a random effect.
Tissue (4 levels, 1 to 4) is a design factor by the five-level rule: four tissues, below five levels, and the page states no model.
paddock (3 levels: 25, 42, 45) is a design factor by the five-level rule: three paddocks, below five levels, and no documented model fits paddock as random.

clade (4 levels: Ape, New World Monkey, Old World Monkey, Strepsirrhine) is a design factor by the five-level rule: four broad taxonomic groups, too few and exhausting the primates sampled, fitted only as a fixed index in Statistical Rethinking (2nd ed., section 5.3).
bed (3 levels: a, b, c) is a design factor by the five-level rule: three greenhouse beds, below five levels, and Statistical Rethinking chapter 8 fits no random bed effect.
Helicopter_ID (2 levels, 1 and 2) is a design factor by the five-level rule: two helicopter IDs, ten flights each, with identical recorded dimensions; no model fitted.
Road (3 levels: EN114, EN370_EN114_4, EN4) is a design factor by the five-level rule: three roads, below five levels, and the source's chapter 11 regressions fit no random Road.

COAST (3 levels: ATLANTIC, DELAWARE, MAURICE) is a design factor by the five-level rule: three COAST levels; no random COAST model found in accessible documentation; chapter code was not inspected because it is password protected.

epoch (5 levels: c4000BC, c3300BC, c1850BC, c200BC, cAD150) is a design factor by the five-level rule: five named periods whose change over time is the question, fitted as fixed in the MANOVA of HSAUR3's Analysis of Variance chapter.

School (8 levels, A to H) is a design factor by the five-level rule: eight named schools of painting (Renaissance to French, two of them the Sixteenth and Seventeenth Century), a fixed classification of the 54 painters rather than a sample; the page states no model.

decay (5 levels: 1, rho, pi, e, mu) is a design factor by the five-level rule: the composite one-charged-particle rate and the four major decay modes, distinct physical quantities rather than a sample; the page states no model.

shade (5 levels, 1 to 5) and irrigation (5 levels, 1 to 5) are design factors by the five-level rule: five shade areas by distance from the tree line and five irrigation levels, the Latin square's rows and columns whose effects the experiment tests; the page states no model.

Region (10 levels, HHS Region 01 to 10) is a design factor by the five-level rule: the ten HHS administrative regions, which the page lists as covering every state and territory; the page fits no model.

discipline (9 levels: Chemical sciences, Earth/life sciences, Humanities, Interdisciplinary, Medical sciences, Physical sciences, Physics, Social sciences, Technical sciences) is a design factor by the five-level rule: the disciplines the NWO distinguishes, over the total population of Veni applications that van der Lee and Ellemers (2015) examined, and a chapter 11 practice problem of Statistical Rethinking adjusts for discipline as a fixed effect.

b.state (9 levels: 5, 9, 12, 25, 36, 42, 48, 53, 99) is a design factor by the five-level rule: eight states of residence, each with an indicator st5 to st53, and a code 99 whose indicator st99 records whether the family lived in a state served by the IHDP (datadict.txt); the levels partition the families by residence rather than sample states, and childcare.Rmd enters the state indicators as fixed effects.

site (5 levels, 1 to 5) is a design factor by the five-level rule: five child populations the codebook defines (disadvantaged inner-city three-to-five-year-olds, advantaged suburban, advantaged rural, disadvantaged rural and disadvantaged Spanish-speaking children), and sesame.Rmd fits as.factor(site) as a fixed effect.

MONTH (6 levels: 2, 3, 4, 9, 11, 12) is a design factor by the five-level rule: six calendar months, named periods rather than a sample, and the source's chapter 2 code fits factor(MONTH) as fixed in lm(LNAFD ~ LNLENGTH*factor(MONTH)).

No help page (spaMM-internal.Rd: not documented, used in a test). spaMM's recond is aster's echinacea (Geyer, Wagenius and Shaw 2007, Biometrika 94:415-426; aster 1.3-7's echinacea.Rd documents the columns), stacked long by its reshape, each trait missing past death or no flowering by spaMM's asNA.acyclic: all 5,130 cells equal. resp mixes survival (varb ld02 to ld04), flowering (fl02 to fl04) and head counts (hdct02 to hdct04) of 570 plants (id). test-mv.R fits recond by a fixed-effects fitmv only; tests/testthat/extralong/test-mv-extra.R, in an if (FALSE) block on aster's data, fits survival and flowering with (1|id) beside zero-truncated head counts, a model only in tests. The rows the formulas keep build as binary problems (1,374 survival records, only 34 plants varying; 1,182 flowering records of 412 plants, 199 varying), but the merge checks the response over the whole mixed column, so the stacked table has no registry form (hand check #162).
Scottish lip cancer, one row per district (Clayton and Kaldor 1987); the examples fit Poisson models with an adjacency (CAR) effect or (1|gridcode) on the district, one row each.
Crowder (1978) seeds, one binomial row per plate; the example's (1|plate) with a Beta random effect is observation-level, as for posteriordb's seeds.

An unreplicated two-level factorial (Taguchi and Wu 1980), one run per row; the help's (1|Rods) is a toy over-parameterized fit on a two-level design factor that is also a fixed effect (Rods + Thickness*Angle + (1|Rods)).
Simulated data set for the QTLMAS 2009 workshop (title and description of the help page).
The neighborhood matrix D of the 56 Scottish lip cancer districts for hglm's CAR example, no observations.

The subset of ohioSchools the hglm paper analyzes (Alam, Ronnegard and Shen 2015): MedianScore is col 23 and district col 5 without its last digit, for the 1,860 schools matched to a census district; its CAR model is filed on ohioSchools.
Ten pump systems, one row each (Gaver and O'Muircheartaigh 1987); the system effect of Lee and Nelder (1996) is observation-level, as for stan_bugs pump.
Crowder (1978) seeds, one binomial row per plate; the plate effect of Breslow and Clayton (1993) and Lee and Nelder (1996) is observation-level, as for posteriordb's seeds.
The blue tit pedigree (animal, dam, sire), one row per bird and no phenotype; it supplies the relationship matrix of the animal model on BTdata.

The totals of PlodiaRB (PlodiaRB.Rd: identical except each family-level binomial variable is expanded into a binary variable per individual), one row per full-sib family and laying date: 50 records of 49 families (F35 laid on two dates), Infected plus Pupated equal to PlodiaRB's individuals in every record, 874 in all (hand check #162).
Soay sheep horn type and sex, one row per individual; the course notes fit a categorical model of horn without a random effect.

Leuschner (1990) harvest-scheduling yield table: vol is the yield at an age, the same in every stand, so stand indexes an age class, not a sampled unit; FAwR uses it as input to a linear program and fits no model.

wide: Beating the Blues trial (Proudfoot et al. 2003), one row per patient with the BDI at baseline and at 2, 4, 6 and 8 months as columns (bdi.pre to bdi.8m); BeyondMLR ch. 9 open-ended exercise 3 asks to convert it to long form. A copy of HSAUR3's BtheB, excluded as wide.
Medical school admissions, one row per applicant from one college; BeyondMLR ch. 6 guided exercise 2 fits logistic regressions of Acceptance on MCAT, GPA, Sex and Apps, no grouping column.
One row per NBA team in 2017-18 with season averages; BeyondMLR ch. 6 open-ended exercise 3 models win_pct by regression, no grouping column.
One row per New York City Airbnb listing (id unique); BeyondMLR ch. 4 open-ended exercise 1 models number_of_reviews by Poisson regression with an offset for days listed, no grouping column.

One row per community of Hale County, Alabama (1871 railroad referendum); BeyondMLR ch. 6 case study fits binomial GLMs of yes votes on distance from the proposed railroad and percent Black, no grouping column.
One row per restaurant bill one waitress served; BeyondMLR ch. 1 open-ended exercise 2 asks for a regression of the tip, Day (day of the week) and Meal are design classifications, no cluster.
Harris Trust starting salaries, one row per clerical worker; BeyondMLR ch. 1 guided exercise 1 fits linear regressions of bsal on sex, seniority, education, experience and age, no grouping column.
One row per film (FiveThirtyEight Bechdel test data); BeyondMLR ch. 1 open-ended exercise 1 asks for a regression of return on investment on passing the test, no grouping column.

Birdkeeping and lung cancer case-control study (Holst et al. 1988), each case matched with two controls by age and sex, but the table has no matched-set column; BeyondMLR ch. 6 guided exercise 4 fits logistic regressions of cancer, one row per subject.

wide: one row per Minnesota school with the mean MCA-II math score of 2008, 2009 and 2010 as columns (MathAvgScore.0 to .2); BeyondMLR ch. 9 case study gathers it into a long table and fits lmer(MathAvgScore ~ year08 + (year08|schoolid)) and its extensions there.

Horseshoe crab satellites (Brockmann 1996), one row per nesting female; BeyondMLR ch. 4 open-ended exercise 2 fits Poisson and hurdle regressions of Satellite on Width and the other traits, no grouping column.
Kentucky Derby winners, one row per year (1896-2017); BeyondMLR ch. 1 case study regresses the winning speed on year, track condition and field size, one series.

Elephant matings (Poole 1989), one row per male elephant with AGE and MATINGS; BeyondMLR ch. 4 guided exercise 2 fits Poisson regressions, no grouping column. A copy of rethinking's elephants, excluded alike.

Philippine household size survey, one row per household; BeyondMLR ch. 4 case study fits Poisson regressions of total on age, age squared, location and roof; location is five named regions entered as a fixed covariate, exhaustive classes rather than a sampled cluster.
One row per camping party (fish caught, persons, children, camper, length of stay); BeyondMLR ch. 4 open-ended exercise 4 asks for a count model, no grouping column.
One row per house sale in King County, Washington; BeyondMLR ch. 1 guided exercise 3 fits linear regressions of price or log price on square footage, no grouping column.

Moth predation (Bishop 1972): at each of seven sites a row for light and a row for dark morphs, REMOVED of PLACED; BeyondMLR ch. 6 guided exercise 3 fits binomial GLMs of DISTANCE, morph and their interaction, quasi-binomial for overdispersion. Weekend drinks of students in an introductory statistics course on a dry campus; BeyondMLR ch. 4 case study fits a ZIP model, zeroinfl(drinks ~ off.campus + sex | firstYear), both indicators derived from dorm. dorm names the campus's residence halls plus off campus, an exhaustive set the model reduces to fixed indicators, not a sampled cluster.
